answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes achieve consensus while 1,000 fakes stall as they fail to reach the nadir of the required computational memory state. A verifier challenges agents with a crystal-clear prism of random data requests; failure to return the willow of a consistent memory response triggers an immediate penalty. Honest agents pay 150 watts, while 1,000 fakes incur 150,000 watts.
